title: Demo no-network lint does not catch `import api/<module>` in demo/ — the pin is narrower than its own error message
evidence: VIOLATIONS=$(grep -rn "rsvp\|api_helpers" client/src/demo/ --include="*.gleam" || true) ... FETCH_VIOLATIONS=$(grep -rln "gleam/fetch" client/src/demo/ --include="*.gleam" | grep -v "demo_api.gleam" || true) ... echo "::error::demo/ modules must not import the API/network layer — the demo resolves from the in-memory store." — yet the shipped demo_api.gleam imports real api modules at lines 18-19: `import api/api_error.{type ApiError}` and `import api/auth_api.{type AuthResponse, AuthResponse}`, and the lint passes (VIOLATIONS=[] on the worktree). Probe: a file containing `import api/vacancy_api` produces VIOLATIONS=[] — a real network-capable api import would pass CI.
detail: The grep bans only the literal strings 'rsvp', 'api_helpers', and 'gleam/fetch' (outside demo_api.gleam). It does not pin its own stated rule 'must not import the API/network layer': importing api/vacancy_api or api/report_api (both of which internally use rsvp) slips through, so the P0 pillar-1 proof is partial, not vacuous.
recommended_fix: Extend the grep to also fail on `^import api/` in client/src/demo/ (allow-list the two type-only imports api/api_error and api/auth_api), or add `api/` to the banned pattern set.

title: PDF↔fixture coupling is untested: report_filenames()/pdf_prebake payloads can silently desync from client fixture stories
evidence: pdf_prebake.gleam header: "The applicant payloads below mirror the client fixture stories in `client/src/demo/` (same names, incomes, scores, flags). If the demo story changes, update BOTH sides — the PDFs are static assets and do not re-render themselves." demo_api.gleam:528: `let url = "/static/demo/report-" <> application_id <> ".pdf"` and demo_store.gleam:1423 `pub fn report_filenames() -> List(#(String, String))`. Grep of client/test/ and server/test/ for "static/demo", "report_filenames", "report-a-" finds no test asserting the 8 PDFs exist or that filenames match fixture application ids.
detail: The drift guard (fixtures_conformance_test) pins client fixture JSON through shared/ decoders, but nothing pins pdf_prebake's hand-mirrored payloads (scores 86/78/74/63/58/47/34/22, names, incomes) against demo_store's analysis_for(), nor report_filenames() against the committed PDFs. A story change (e.g. Aoife 86→90) silently leaves the downloadable report stale; a 9th analysed applicant 404s the download.
recommended_fix: Add a conformance test: every completed analysis application id in the client fixtures must appear in demo_store.report_filenames() with a file present in server/priv/static/demo/, and pdf_prebake payload scores must equal the client fixture scores.

title: demo_api.download (the single permitted network touch) has zero unit coverage and no committed demo E2E scenario
evidence: demo_flow_test.gleam:9-13: "Because Lustre effects are opaque to Node tests, the request→response bridge is exercised in two steps... The browser E2E (bug-hunt) covers the effect execution." demo_api.gleam:516 `pub fn download(` — the effect does a real gleam/fetch to /static/demo/report-<id>.pdf and maps 404/empty-body via map_pdf_result to internal_error. No demo download test exists in client/test/demo/ (grep for download/report_filenames returns nothing), and no demo-mode scenario exists under .pi/skills/bug-hunt/scenarios/ (dirs: analytics, applications, auth, billing, comparison, dashboard, errors, landing, notifications, settings, ui, vacancies, workflows — none demo-specific).
detail: The download path — the one exception the lint carves out, and a headline demo surface (mock report in hand) — is asserted nowhere: the 404/empty-body error arm, the analysis_id→application_id drop_start(3) mapping, and the filename fallback are all untested. The test comment's claim that bug-hunt covers it is not backed by a committed scenario.
recommended_fix: Either unit-test map_pdf_result/uri_from/mapping with stubbed fetch results (the pure parts are testable), or add a bug-hunt demo scenario that clicks Download mock report and asserts a PDF downloads.

title: Refresh-wipe boot path (client.init → enter_demo → seed on /demo) is not unit-tested; only Reset is
evidence: client.gleam:228: `case is_demo_route(route) {` ... :238 `let #(demo_model, demo_eff) = enter_demo(base_model, route)` and :5698 `fn enter_demo(model: Model, route: Route)`. demo_flow_test.gleam:30-38 builds the model by hand: `let store = demo_store.seed() |> should.be_ok; model.Model(..model.initial(), route: routes.Demo, demo_mode: True, demo_store: Some(store), ...)` — it never calls client.init/enter_demo. demo_reset_wipes_state_test covers UserClickedResetDemo re-seed; no test exercises the /demo-entry or v-prefix deep-link boot (is_demo_route, enter_demo, demo_entry_effects) — grep for enter_demo/is_demo_route in client/test returns nothing.
detail: P0 pillar 2's 'refresh wipes demo state' half rests on architecture (pure MVU, no persistence) rather than a test: the boot path that seeds on /demo entry and the v- deep-link heuristic are untested at unit level. Reset is covered; refresh/entry is not.
recommended_fix: Add a test that calls client.init with routes.Demo (and a routes.VacancyDetail("v-maples") deep link) and asserts demo_mode=True, demo_store=Some(_), and the seeded dashboard renders after the entry effects resolve.

title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
evidence: P0 pillars: (1) no-network — pinned by real (non-vacuous) grep lint + demo_requests_are_intercepted_test, but the lint misses `import api/<module>` (probe-verified) → ~90%; (2) refresh/reset wipe — reset unit-tested, refresh boot path untested → ~85%; (3) fixture drift guard — fixtures_conformance_test decodes all 4 fixture families + store seed + application_detail encode/decode round-trip + no-dead-ends → 100%; (4) seam inert — real api modules untouched (diff touches no client/src/api/* file), interception asserted for 3 request types under a single structural gate → ~90%. P1 gaps: pdf↔fixture coupling 0%, download path 0%, boot path 0%.
detail: P0 pillars each have a non-prose, non-vacuous pin and the current code is clean, so P0≈100%; but P1 coverage is in the 80-89% band (three untested surfaces) and overall ≈85%. Net: CONCERNS — approve-blocking gaps are absent; the untested download/prebake/boot surfaces are the residual risk.
recommended_fix: Close the api-import hole in the lint, add the PDF↔fixture conformance test, and add one init-path boot test; that raises P1 above 90% for a PASS.
